title: `PageHeaderProps.actions` declares `z.array(z.string())` but objectui's canonical `page:header` renderer consumes ActionDef objects — satisfying the schema deletes every header button
body:
Filed **unassigned** by the `repo:hotcrm` execution seat — a platform gap found while building the exemplar app, filed at destination per that lane's charter (「平台相关的功能应该在平台中实现」). Not a claim, and not a seam card: the defect is entirely inside the platform, and hotcrm is only where it was noticed.

Consumer-side record: objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1279 (blocked on this).

## The disagreement

`PageHeaderProps.actions` in `@objectstack/spec` is:

```ts
actions: z.array(z.string())   // "Action IDs"
```

objectui's canonical `page:header` renderer consumes ActionDef **objects**. Measured at objectui's pinned SHA:

- it filters the array through `actionRendersAt(a, 'record_header')` — a string has no `.locations`, so every entry is filtered out;
- it reads `a.requiredPermissions`, `a.visible`, `a.name`, `a.order`;
- every test it ships (`page-header-actions.test.tsx`) authors objects.

So the two faces cannot both be satisfied by one authored value. **The schema and the thing that renders disagree**, and the source can only conform to one.

## Why this is not "just an unenforced key"

`PageComponent.properties` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`, so a mismatched value is **dropped rather than refused** — the page builds, the artifact writes, the component renders. That makes this the expensive direction: an author who *conforms to the declaration* silently loses the feature.

Measured in the exemplar: hotcrm authors **16 header actions across 4 record pages**, all declaring `locations: ['record_header', …]`, all rendering today (confirmed in `dist/objectstack.json`). Rewriting them as ids to satisfy the schema would turn the conformance guard green **and delete every header button** — Convert Lead, Generate Quote, Escalate Case, and the activity trio.

A change that turns a gate green while removing a feature is the worst shape this class can take, because the gate then certifies the loss.

## Why it is filed here rather than in the app

Both routes out are platform-side:

1. **objectui gains a lookup-by-name path** — `record:quick_actions` already has one, so this is an existing pattern rather than a new mechanism, and it would make the spec's stated shape actually work.
2. **The spec widens** to accept ActionDef objects, per its own #5611/#6276 rule that the delivered shape is the contract.
3. (App-side, and what hotcrm does today: keep authoring objects, warn, and carry an exemption. That is a workaround for a platform disagreement, which the exemplar's charter forbids as a permanent answer.)

Choosing between 1 and 2 is a platform ruling, and I have deliberately not assumed one.

## A secondary cost, recorded because it is easy to miss

Because ActionDefs are **inlined into page properties**, their whole script bodies ship in the built artifact — hotcrm's is 1.9 MB. Whichever route is taken, route 1 would also remove that: an id reference does not carry a body.

## Related

- objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1279 — the consumer-side card, `pm:blocked` on this one.
- objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1269 / PR #1280 — the conformance sweep that surfaced it; this class is **excluded** there with an exemption line naming this issue, precisely so nobody "fixes" it into green.
- objectstack#11289 — the same declared-vs-delivered disagreement pointing the *other* way (`record:details` sections honour `collapsible` in the renderer while the strict section schema rejects it). Two instances suggests the class is worth a sweep of `ComponentPropsMap` against its renderers, not just two point fixes.
